docs.text: Zebrasoma gemmatum ¶ Result: fail ¶ Arrival Notes / Origin / Price ¶ One of the nicest gem tangs I've seen. Looks great, but has a pinched belly. Initial diagnoses ¶ Possible internal parasites, but should not be too much of an issue. Initial prognosis ¶ Should be a straightforward QT. Day 1 ¶ Drip acclimated, then gave the fish an H2O2 bath. Fed the fish, and he ate a bit of the food, but not very aggressively. Dosed up copper, and noticed a couple spots on the fish, but not a concerning amount. Day 2 ¶ Woke up and checked on him. Found him laying on the floor of the tank, completely covered in spots. Eyes are cloudy, and the fish looks completely morribund. We created a makeshift oxygen generator with potatos + hydrogen peroxide to help him breathe. A few hours after adding some O2, he can swim on his own for a brief period of time. video When we went to bed, he seemed like he was in a decent state. I am optimistic he will recover. Day 3 ¶ Woke up to find the tang did not make it through the night. Very disappointing, but I look forward to the next one, but will be starting him in full copper immediately instead of waiting for a few hours. Conclussions: ¶ Given the timeline of this fish's demise, I think this guy suffered from marine velvet. I was very impressed by how effective the potato oxygen was, and may use this trick in the future if a similar situation is encountered. Similar fish: ¶ n / a

docs.text: 01/08/2025 ¶ Result: fail ¶ Arrival Notes ¶ Rather large, adult specimen. Specimen came in 3 gallons of (pretty dirty) water bag was lined with korean newspaper, I wonder if he was drop-shipped. Initial diagnoses ¶ Has some ich visible, but a manageable amount Belly is definitely pinched, which makes me very nervous Initial prognosis ¶ While the pinched belly is pretty worrying, I'm optimistic. Day 1 ¶ Specimen arrived via AA cargo, after ~12 hours transit. After drip acclimation, he was placed in a methylene blue + formalin bath for 30 minutes After bath, placed in a tank by himself with air stone + PVC + sponge filter Due to visible ich, I pre-dosed the water to 2.5 ppm copper + 300 mg nitrofurazone. Fed brine shrimp soaked in metro / kanaplex. He ate somewhat well, but not super aggresively. this inspired confidence, as he ate in full copper + ate medicated Frist night was a formalin dose Day 2 ¶ Eating less aggressively, possibly not at all. Breathing seems labored, but not aggressive. The water is somewhat cloudy, so I performed a 5 gallon water change, pre-dosed with copper + sucked out as much food as I could from the bottom Day 3 ¶ Still not eating much, but the food seems to disappear. I added nori on a clip to see if he'd go for that, but he seemed disinterested. He swims around in a pattern: leave PVC towards the center, swim up a bit, turn around, swim through PVC, rotate (awkwardly) in the corner, and repeat. Day 4 ¶ Woke up around 6 AM for a frag swap, came down to find the tang dead. He was floating at the top of the tank with his mouth facing up. He was alive and looking normal when Ruxin added prazipro before we went to bed ~1 AM. I unfortunately didn't look at the fish before I went upstairs, as I was focused on the swap. Conclussions: ¶ I'm not sure what happened, honestly. I never saw any tang poops. I saw some stringy white excriment leaving him, but it was not long enough for me to think internal worms. Most likely internal flagellates. Other than disease, ammonia could have played a factor. The fact that this guy died at night and was found at the surface could mean lack of O2, but I did not see unusual breathing from this guy, other than the somewhat labored breathes. Similar fish: ¶ This one reminded me of the first time we QT'd a gem tang .

docs.text: 01/22/2025 ¶ Result: TBD ¶ Arrival Notes ¶ Large, adult specimen. ~6" Specimen came in his own box with 4+ gallons of water Initial diagnoses ¶ Belly is definitely pinched, which makes me very nervous (especially after last time ). Initial prognosis ¶ While the pinched belly is pretty worrying, I'm optimistic. Day 1 (01/22/2025) ¶ Specimen arrived via AA cargo Drip acclimated for a little over an hour. Given a methylene blue + formalin bath for 30 minutes After bath, placed in a tank by himself with fluidized media, PVC, and a sponge Dosed Chloroquine phosphate at 65 mg / gallon Fed brine shrimp soaked in metro / kanaplex. He ate pretty well Day 2 (01/23/2025) ¶ Eating aggressively, looking quite good. The water is somewhat cloudy. Re-dosed chloroquine phosphate, 5 mg / gallon Day 3 (01/24/2025) ¶ Still eating really well, but not defecating. out of concern, I made a thread here Humble said this happens sometimes for malnurished fish, which checks out with the pinched belly. Holding back concern for now. Changed water + re-dosed CP. Day 4 (01/25/2025) ¶ Formalin bath #2 Still eating very well, but is doing a bit of scratching. I think Flukes is possible, but very unlikely (due to the formalin baths) dosed prazipro out of an abundance of caution Day 5 (01/26/2025) ¶ Water is getting cloudy again, planning on a water change tomorrow. Still scratching some From what I have been able to find, this is a side-effect of CP. It could be that he's just itchy. Since we have been doing the formalin baths, I'm not worried about the flukes taking hold, and will not dose any more prazipro. Day 6 (01/27/2025) ¶ Conclussions: ¶

docs.text: 01/08/2025 ¶ Result: Success ¶ Initial diagnoses ¶ Strange growth on side of mouth. Not sure what it is. Initial prognosis ¶ Should be only as difficult as normal wrasses are Day 1 ¶ Typical fairy wrasse behavior. Eats decently well Day 2 ¶ Spends most of the day hiding Copper tested at 2.9, so we did a partial change to reduce to 2.5 ppm. Day 5 (1/12/2025) ¶ 100% water change + formalin bath Day 6 (1/13/2025) ¶ Strange growth still visible, but seems to be the best of the bunch so far Day 14 (1/22/2025) ¶ Customer grabbed the wrasses ~1 day earlier than I'd like, but they were technically in copper for 14 days. The first day was at ~1.5 ppm, so I'm okay with this. The fish still has the strange growth on his face, but I think it should go away pretty quickly. QT M8's ¶ Lineatus Exquisitus

docs.text: 01/08/2025 ¶ Result: Success ¶ Initial diagnoses ¶ Nothing obvious Initial prognosis ¶ Should be only as difficult as normal wrasses are Day 1 ¶ Typical fairy wrasse behavior. Ate on the first day Day 2 ¶ Spends most of the day hiding Copper tested at 2.9, so we did a partial change to reduce to 2.5 ppm. Day 5 (1/12/2025) ¶ 100% water change + formalin bath Specimen is visibly struggling before bath During the bath, the specimen does not seem to be able to swim. Current from the air stone can move the fish around, and the fish does not resist being handled / moved Post-bath the specimen continues to struggle Laying on the floor upside down, not controlling balance, not eating Day 6 (1/13/2025) ¶ Specimen is upright in the middle of the tank, but not hiding at all. Remains stationary in mucous sack Day 7 (1/14/2025) ¶ Specimen's behavior is actually surprisingly normal, and is eating Excriment is either normal, or a white stringy substance Remarkable recovery given the state this fish was in only a few days prior Day 14 ¶ Customer picked up the fish a day earlier than anticipated, but we did get a full 14 days in copper. Overall, I'm certain this fish would not have made it without QT, and I'm thrilled with the results. QT M8's ¶ Bluehead Fairy Wrasse Exquisitus
